text:
Sara: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a "soft cursor" approach for SDKs: prefer streaming/resumable cursors when available, but automatically fall back to page-based polling with a small client-side state (last-seen-id + window) when transport doesn't support resume. tradeoffs?

Kevin: I like the practicality. main concerns: semantics across py/ts/go and idempotency if a page fetch overlaps. we need a clear contract for last-seen semantics.

Mina: agree. also watch for duplicated items vs missing items. typical pattern: fetch page, dedupe by id client-side and advance cursor after stable ack.

Ellen: what about retries? if we retry a page fetch on 5xx, should the SDK apply exponential backoff or keep strict bounds so apps don't see long stalls?

Kevin: exponential backoff with jitter for 5xx; immediate retry for transient network hiccups (tcp reset) but limit to 2 fast retries. documentable policy per-language.

Mina: nit: for long-poll endpoints we should prefer 'resume token' semantics (opaque token from server) over last-seen-id where possible. tokens allow server-side compaction. but tokens complicate offline resumption across versions.

Sara: proposed default for SDKs: 1) prefer resume token when server exposes one; 2) fall back to client soft-cursor (last-seen-id + window) otherwise; 3) on fallback enable dedupe and idempotent apply hooks.

Kevin: compatibility across languages: implement same state machine but idiomatic APIs per language. API shape idea:

```
// pseudocode
cursor = client.listItems.streamableCursor({pageSize: 200})
for (chunk in cursor) {
  handle(chunk)
}
// if streamableCursor falls back the iterator still yields pages the same way
```

Mina: love that. important to expose the 'mode' for debugging: "stream" | "poll" | "resume-token" in the cursor object so users and observability can tell what happened.

Ellen: observability note: console should record per-route fallback events and counts so customers can see how often they hit poll fallback (helps capacity/serve changes).

Sara: about transport choices: should python/ts default to WebSocket for long-lived resume, and go default to gRPC streams? both need a consistent reconnect/resume backoff.

Kevin: yes but hide transport behind the cursor abstraction. let language runtimes choose best underlying transport. long-term we want a single wire resume protocol: token + last-offset. gRPC streaming and WS can both encode it.

Mina: error handling: define canonical error classes across SDKs (RetryableTransient, NonRetryableClient, ResumeNotSupported). then transports map underlying errors to them.

Ellen: for paginated endpoints that also support streaming, we should provide a convenience shim that returns an async iterator but internally switches to streaming when available. users get consistent ergonomics.

Kevin: security/observability: when resume tokens are used, rotate and short-live tokens so stolen tokens have limited exposure. note this affects client offline resume windows.

Sara: action items: (1) draft spec for soft-cursor state machine with edgecases (overlap, hole detection, dedupe window) — Mina to own; (2) sketch API shapes for py/ts/go showing iterator/async-iterator/chan forms — Kevin to own; (3) add telemetry events for fallback counts + transport mode — Ellen to own.

ci-bot: build #3421 started for sdk-iterable-fallback-tests :construction:

Mina: will mock server that returns resume tokens + a fallback path. will add regression tests for duplication and missing-range scenarios.

Kevin: +1. let's sync Wed 10am to review the draft and api sketches.

Sara: thanks all — this should make SDKs more robust in heterogeneous infra environments. :thumbsup:
